newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firmer with the December confederate bond futures contract rising back to its highest levels since October 22.

The contract moved through the October 23 high of 115.21 late in the day to close at 115.25, the highest level since the October 22 high of 115.29. Prices were helped by the Swiss franc's stronger tone on currency markets. Activity was quiet with U.S. bond markets closed for Veteran's Day.
The dollar only got up to 1.2663 francs Monday in Europe, below 1.2850, the 21-month peak set November 6. The mark dipped towards 84.00 centimes from an 84.37 high set on Friday.
Swiss bonds also firmed with respect to German Bunds. The 10-year yield spread YLDS3 widened slightly to back over 200 basis points from levels closer to 190 last week.
Short-term rates were lower, with the March three-month EuroSwiss contract traded on LIFFE also ending at its highs of the day, and at its highest levels in over a week.

In early afternoon the Swiss National Bank (SNB) released statistics on reserves activity for the 10-day period in early November which showed the level of sight deposits increased. An SNB spokesman said that the data showed the SNB was remaining flexible in meeting banks' demand for liquidity.
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 up 50 points at 115.25.
Dec Comi bond COMIZ6 up 18 points at 110.25.
Mar Euro Swiss francs FESM7 up 11 points at 97.83.
